storage: append-only JSONL day-files under <archive>/cbpborderwait/ by CAPTURE date (gz after 2 days)
written_by: server/cbpBorderWait.ts archiveBorderWaits (hourly poll; change-only dedup keeps quiet hours nearly free; eager boot)
source: CBP Border Wait Times, bwt.cbp.gov/api/bwtnew — keyless JSON, 83 land crossings. NOTE: the RSS path probed at filing serves an HTML SPA (status-200 probes are not body probes — lesson recorded); bwtnew is the real feed. Verified live 2026-07-05
license: US government work, public domain; attribution 'CBP Border Wait Times'

field_map.port_number|crossing|lane|values — dedup: an unchanged wait re-polled hourly writes nothing; every change appends
field_map.lane: commercial_standard | commercial_FAST | passenger_standard (flattened per lane class; a crossing WITHOUT commercial lanes contributes no commercial rows — real, not missing)
field_map.delay_min/lanes_open: numeric, locale-independent; empty published values are null, never zero
field_map.status/border/update_time: ARCHIVED VERBATIM and LOCALIZED BY SERVING REGION (our probe egress received Spanish; prod may receive English) — parsing never keys on these strings; joins use port_number

confidence_model: RAW official operational data. Fills the ROAD leg of the freight-proxy set (sea=AIS, rail=STB, air=ADS-B). HYPOTHESIS (gate-locked): sustained commercial wait anomalies at top freight crossings (Laredo, Otay Mesa, El Paso) lead border-dependent logistics/intermodal volumes — prior ~20%, transmission is indirect; archive-first.
geo_fields: (port_number -> coordinates needs a port-of-entry table; map layer deferred with the FAA one)
cadence: hourly poll (waits move intra-day at commercial crossings)
